The quicksort algorithm works by selecting a pivot element and partitioning
the array around it. Elements less than the pivot go to the left partition,
elements greater go to the right. The algorithm then recursively sorts each
partition. Average time complexity is O(n log n), though worst case is O(n^2)
when the pivot is consistently poor, such as sorting an already-sorted array
with a first-element pivot strategy. Randomized or median-of-three pivot
selection makes the worst case vanishingly unlikely in practice. Space
complexity is O(log n) for the recursion stack in the in-place variant.
